This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Order (September
22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will
be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be live
streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to bsaleaumu a@ malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency,
as well as states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of
California, and a federal emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to
reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but
conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees. This way the public, the staff, and the Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which are
not listed on the agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action
may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing
response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak during the
meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration.
Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to
the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar
will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first
will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow
the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above
are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
bsaleaumua@malibucitv.org.

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department in February 2023.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in February 2023.

RECREATION

Aquatics: The Malibu Community Pool was closed from January 30 through February 12
due to a malfunctioning water pump. Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District
(SMMUSD) replaced the pump, and the City resumed operating hours on February 13.
  1
On February 6, spring registration opened for the swim team and Master s adult
conditioning. There are currently forty pre-registered swim team participants and six adult
conditioning swimmers.

Community Classes: Winter community and afterschool programs continued through
February and included creative workshops, parent and me classes, and youth programs.
Popular programs include animal adventures, ballet, barre fitness, chess , hip hop, mega
machines, musical theater, secret science agents, soccer, and Tai Chi.

Recreation Guide: The Spring 2023 Recreation Guide and City Newsletter was mailed to
Malibu residents on February 6. The Guide features the Department's programs and parks
and includes informative articles and contact information for City departments and
services. Program registration opened on February 13. Staff had an informational booth

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 on February 11 at Malibu Bluffs Park and provided copies of the Recreation Guide and a
giveaway bag.

Seniors: Weekly Senior recreation programs continued in the Senior Center at City Hall
and at Malibu Bluffs Park. Existing programs include art, ballet, broadway jazz dance,
cardio salsa, chair yoga, choir, coloring, knitting, mat yoga, Pilates, and stretch and
strength.

On February 9, Tressa Thompson, Driver Safety Manager from the Department of Motor
Vehicles, led a Senior Driver Safety educational lecture for 19 attendees. Participants
learned about the Driver's License renewal process, the REAL ID, how to get an
identification card, and Disabled Placards. Refreshments were provided for the workshop.

On February 16, Jamie Hilbert, a Nurse Practitioner with the Malibu Medical Group,
presented a Heart Health educational lecture highlighting February as American Heart
Health month. Seniors learned about blood pressure, heart health, diet, and exercise
habits. Refreshments were provided for the workshop.

On February 23, Recreation staff hosted a Valentine's Day Sweetheart Soiree-themed
luncheon for 64 participants. Attendees enjoyed lunch from Mendocino Farms and
watched a performance by juggler and comedian, David Cousin. The Key, a home care
assistance organization, provided desserts and pastries from Porto's Bakery.

Skate: The winter Learn to Skate program, instructed by Champ Camp for children ages
6 through 12, had maximum capacity attendance of twenty-five participants. Instructors
subdivided the group based on ability and skating technique.

On February 19, instructors from Champ Camp led a Girl's Skateboarding Clinic for six
participants who learned the fundamental skills of skateboarding. The clinic was part of
the "Play Like a Girl Malibu" program to encourage female sports participation.

Social Media: Department's social media featured arts programs, community classes,
senior programs, spring program registration, and the Student Art Exhibit closing
reception. Social media analytics indicated 1,324 accounts were reached on lnstagram
through "views" and "sharing posts." Women aged thirty-five through forty-four were the
main demographic viewing the posts. lnstagram "views" increased by 45% from January
2023.

Special Events: Park Tales "Let's Go Fly a Kite," in partnership with the Malibu Library,
occurred on February 9. Ten families received a goodie bag with City program flyers,
snacks, stickers, and an art activity donated by the Malibu Library.

The 2023 Student Art Exhibit Closing Reception was on February 26. Over one-hundred
student artists from Webster Elementary School, Malibu Elementary School, Malibu
Middle School, Malibu High School, and Our Lady of Malibu School were featured in the
show.
  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 Sports: The Youth and Middle School Basketball Leagues concluded on February 10 and
11. Fifty players in grades sixth through eighth participated in the Middle School division,
and seventy players in the Youth division for grades kindergarten through fifth. Staff
distributed a league evaluation survey to gain feedback and recommendations to
incorporate into the 2023-2024 Basketball League.

PARK MAINTENANCE

Equestrian Park: Staff removed dirt and debris from drains and v-ditches throughout the
park that accumulated after rain events.

Filled a sinkhole with topsoil located near the park restrooms.

Legacy Park: Burns Pacific Construction began repair work on the walkway pavers.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Replaced two display cases on the special events storage containers.

Marked all irrigation sprinklers and valve boxes on the Multipurpose Field in preparation
for Malibu Little League temporary backstop installation.

Replaced two playground rules signs with updated signage.

Replaced skatelite surface panels and removed graffiti throughout the skate park. Touch-
up paint was also applied to repair structured areas.

Michael Landon Center: Repaired, cleaned, and lubricated the lock on the office door.

Removed graffiti from various areas in exterior restrooms.

Installed signage in the activity room stating, "please do not touch mirrors."

Replaced the HVAC air filter in the activity room.

Replaced a broken wall-mounted sleeve in the men's restroom.

Trancas Canyon Park: Due to significant rain in February, the Multipurpose Field was
closed. Maintenance staff inspected the field daily, and once the field conditions were safe
and dry, the field was reopened.

Staff removed dirt and debris from drains and v-ditches throughout the park that
accumulated after rain events.

Raised an electrical box below grade on the Multipurpose Field turf to meet standards.

Subject:  Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve a recommendation nominating Sara Wan as the
recipient of the 2023 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award for City Council consideration.

DISCUSSION: At the February 23, 2023 Special meeting, the Commission reviewed the
nomination process and potential 2023 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award nominees. By
consensus, the Commission chose not to open the public nomination process and
selected Sara Wan as the 2023 recipient.

Mrs. Wan was a Malibu resident and served on the California Coastal Commission and
the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy board. She focused on conservation and public
beach access across California and was considered an expert in habitat and wetland
issues, marine mammal issues, water quality, and coastal land planning. Additionally, Mrs.
Wan helped provide opportunities for underserved youth to participate in recreation
throughout the region . Mrs. Wan passed away in September 2022; she was 83 years old.

Once the Commission approves Sara Wan as the 2023 recipient, the City Council will
consider the recommendation at an upcoming meeting.

Subject:  Mentorship Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss and provide feedback on a mentorship program.

DISCUSSION: The Parks and Recreation Commission was given an assignment by the
City Council to provide recommendations for a mentorship program and docent programs
to incorporate community leaders, retired professionals, athletes, business owners, .or
college students.

In 2010, the City received a donation from the National Football League (NFL) and
organized sports clinics and mentorship opportunities, including incorporating the "Play
Like A Girl Malibu" initiative to encourage female sports participation. With the NFL
donation, the City organized several programs for girls, including sports clinics with
celebrated professional athletes Jessica Mendoza (softball), Candace Parker (basketball),
and Kerri Walsh-Jennings (volleyball). Since 2011 , the City has offered over 100 "Play
Like a Girl Malibu" programs, and in 2023 there will be clinics in skateboarding, water polo,
tennis, soccer, and surfing.

From 2010 to 2022, Pepperdine University student-athletes have volunteered at various
City programs, including Tiny Tot Olympics, Park Tales, and sports classes. Athletes led
sports stations, discussed health and mental wellness, and read sports-related stories to
community class participants.

The Commission may discuss opportunities for a mentorship program while considering
available staff time for adding new programs. Items for discussion may include potential
guidelines, program partners, an application process, and other items that may enhance
the program .
